subject: Game Theory
title: The War of Attrition
description: A micro-lesson that makes The War of Attrition usable.

hook.text: Two animals want the same territory. Neither attacks—they just wait, burning energy until one quits.

buildup.text: The longer you wait, the more energy you waste. But quitting means losing the prize entirely.

discovery.text: The optimal strategy is random: commit to waiting a random time. No fixed rule can be exploited.

twist.text: If your opponent knows your limit, they wait one second longer. Randomness prevents exploitation.

climax.text: Real animals do this: staring contests, roaring matches, and display fights are wars of attrition.

punchline.text: Sometimes the best strategy is random.

quiz.question: Why is randomness optimal in a war of attrition?
